admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. For purpose=agent_control the immutable accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision is resolved by its whole-value claim of retype(this EventId, realm); the genesis MUST NOT carry a backward agent_provision ref, which would create an EventId cycle. The verifier cross-binds the complete actor/controller AccountIds, PCR delegation and provision payload before materializing Agent status. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch proves its separate accepted organization authority. A self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact account ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the root-round responder; glare branch: the full signed request Event author ActorId referenced by requests[0], never the Station receipt issuer_id; requests MUST be strictly ascending by the complete request_event_ref wire string UTF-8 unsigned bytes, with duplicate Event refs rejected regardless of receipt digest and no receiver-side sorting or deduplication), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.sidecar_account_self_authored_proof: Admitted only when Event actor_id is the account branch and its complete AccountId is the authenticated controller account. The reducer derives controller_account_id byte-for-byte from actor_id.account_id, uses (realm_id, controller_account_id) as the singleton key, and rejects the service actor branch with sidecar_create_denied before revealing existence. The same exact AccountId binds Sidecar membership, MLS genesis and participant authority; principal-only equality is forbidden.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry and resolve to exactly one closed payload schema.
An accepted durable Event becomes shared history only when the current authority includes its exact bytes in a signed RealmCommit for the Event's own Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream.
Stream identity is derived from the Event's closed scope. Realm, each Circle, and each Sidecar have independent commit streams; no Realm-global total chain exists.
Event carries no chain predecessor or authority-commit proof. Only RealmCommit carries previous_commit_ref, and only within the same stream.
Reducers derive typed current results by replaying committed Events in stream position order. Account-private material is outside shared authority-commit streams.

result_writes[] is the machine contract for which typed current results one Event kind writes, in what order, and under which closed condition; zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 10 read it as the source of truth, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_contracts validates every declared row: a declared value_projection member MUST be declared by that row's value_schema_ref, and a whole-value set MUST write every member that schema requires. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND THIS IS A KNOWN GAP: 61 of the 140 reducer_input kinds declare it; the remaining 79 still have no machine-readable reducer contract, so their registered writes exist only in prose. The declaring kinds are deliberately not enumerated here: event_kinds[] already is that list, the enumeration that used to sit in this sentence went stale behind it, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_coverage_note now recomputes both counts from the rows and fails when this sentence disagrees. Normative prose MUST NOT cite result_writes[] for a kind that does not declare it -- a citation without a row is the exact defect this array was added to close. The converse obligation binds a declaring kind: a kind's rows MUST enumerate EVERY typed current result its accepted admission writes on the shared face, so a kind that writes four families and declares one describes itself wrongly in the artifact readers are told is the source of truth. That obligation cannot be gated here, because the lint has no second list of a kind's writes to compare a row set against; it is normative in zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1 and it is why a kind with atomic multi-family writes lands all of them in one batch or none. Extend coverage kind by kind and shrink this note; do not narrow the rule to make it read as complete.

transition_contracts declares the lifecycle axis of a typed current result family: its closed state set, its entry idiom (exactly one of initial_state / initial_states / template), its terminal states and its allowed (from, to) edges. tools/artifact_lint:fsm_reachability reads it together with every transition result_projection and requires that each declared state be reachable from the entry set, that each allowed edge have a write that can perform it, that no const edge leave the table and that no terminal state carry an outgoing edge. A family that declares a machine MUST NOT be written by any non-transition projection: a set installs a state without passing the table, which would make allowed_transitions documentation rather than a rule. Between the authority-commit clean break and 2026-09-18 this block did not exist while the gate still read it under the removed cell_* names, so check reported success over four normative paragraphs (zh/models/circle.md, zh/models/morph.md, zh/models/realm-and-space.md, zh/models/strand-and-message.md) that name transition_contracts as the source of truth for object lifecycle transitions; an absent or empty block is now a failure. Those four object families are themselves still unregistered, so their archive / restore lifecycle has no machine contract yet -- that is a coverage gap, not a licence to read the prose as satisfied.

payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form declared by each id_kind row.

Storage implementations MAY store producer-allocated raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The payload construction MUST be fixed by that kind's id_form and identity_authority columns, never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses UUIDv7; event_derived uses the creating Event's 33-byte token; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest-suite code followed by the complete 32-byte digest under its registered kind-specific preimage contract. v1 Event and suite-tagged identities accept only registered active suite codes with high nibble 0x0; this constraint does not give that nibble any meaning beyond the suite code. A UUID version nibble or digest-suite byte alone never proves identity authority.

A producer_allocated UUIDv7 is never a globally sufficient protocol identity. Its canonical identity key is (mint_authority, typed_id), where mint_authority is the DID whose accepted proof authorized the first durable appearance of that ID. Bare typed-ID lookup, cross-authority deduplication, and last-writer-wins collision repair are forbidden.

Storage implementations MAY store producer_allocated UUID values as raw 16-byte UUIDs. Event-derived and suite-tagged full-digest IDs MUST instead store their raw 33-byte token; they MUST NOT use a native UUID column.

The id_form is fixed by registry kind and never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses RFC 9562 UUIDv7; event_derived uses the same canonical 33-byte token as its creating Event ID; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest suite code followed by all 32 digest octets. Both token forms serialize as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters.

A database MAY intern any full Realm wire identity in a canonical Realm table and use a database-local surrogate pk for joins, indexes, and foreign keys. That pk is never serialized or signed. The canonical table MUST retain a unique lossless 33-byte Realm identity (or its full typed wire form), and every realm_pk foreign key MUST resolve to the same wire Realm identity carried by the protocol record.

Every special_forms row declares payload_pattern, the machine-readable value space of everything after its ak:<kind>: prefix; wire_form remains the human-readable template and payload_pattern is its only normative expansion. A schema, OpenAPI or profile carrier MAY be narrower than payload_pattern for a specific field, but MUST NOT accept an octet payload_pattern rejects, and MUST end-anchor so no trailing byte escapes the declared value space.

producer_allocated_identity_contract.security_rationale: UUIDv7 randomness and timestamp layout do not authenticate the allocator. Binding every producer-selected ID to the accepted genesis signer prevents an attacker from claiming another producer's ID by copying or predicting the UUID.

issuer_record_identity_contract.v1_suite_code_constraint: The complete uint8 suite wire code is encoded unchanged, but v1 accepts only registered active codes whose high nibble is 0x0; this is not a Realm derivation-class nibble.

closed_encoding.audience_id: canonical_bare_resource_service_did; never an HTTP origin or endpoint URL
closed_encoding.credential_binding: credential_class is standard or recovery_session; holder_binding is required; device_binding is required only for standard human_device and forbidden for recovery_candidate_device and agent_runtime

issuer_record_identity_contract.signed_claim_binding: Every preimage field except fixed schema is a signed JWT claim, including credential_class and holder_binding; kind is the fixed credential kind and jti is the derived typed ID. Verifiers MUST reconstruct the complete preimage from signed claims and recompute jti, so different credential classes or holder bindings cannot share one valid ID.
issuer_record_identity_contract.session_chain_rule: session_id is independently allocated before first issuance, refresh inherits it, and it MUST NOT equal or derive from grant_id
issuer_record_identity_contract.device_id_rule: No independent top-level device_id claim enters the preimage; standard human holder_binding and its complete device_binding carry accepted-device authority. Recovery candidate-device and Agent runtime holder bindings carry their own device_id and forbid device_binding.

lifecycle.refresh: one issuer transaction creates active successor and supersedes predecessor with successor_session_grant_id

account_status_record_identity_contract.digest_input: SHA-256(JCS(record fields excluding account_status_record_id and proof))
account_status_record_identity_contract.sequence_rule: status_seq starts at 1; seq=1 is active and has no previous_account_status_record_id; every successor is current+1 and names the exact current account_status_record_id

realm_token_layout.event_derived_retype_identity: Realm and Event token headers are identical, so an ak.realm.create Event token is byte-identical to its Realm token and retyping only swaps the ak:event: / ak:realm: prefix. v1 Realm identity is fixed to SHA-256, so only a creating Event with header 0x01 is Realm-eligible.
realm_token_layout.high_nibble_carries_no_category: The high nibble is reserved zero and carries no category information. Realm purpose lives in the signed create payload; implementations MUST NOT infer purpose from realm_id.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference using an active digest-suite id (v1: sha256 or profile-gated blake3); distinct from ak:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs. The embedded digest is the sole wire carrier of the referenced bytes' digest; same-carrier sibling digest mirrors are forbidden (encoding.md 4.0.1).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical value for equality and indexing; generic consumers MUST NOT split or normalize the adapter-defined core segment.
special_forms.description: Stable DID-derived principal, actor or service identity core. It is not a DID, is not directly resolvable, and MUST be projected only by a registered DID method adapter from a canonical bare did. Registered as a special form rather than an id_form because its identity authority is the external DID method, not an Arkret producer or Event digest.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte delegation digest or the complete typed content-addressed reference; the reference is the only wire carrier of that digest.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed membership-compensation delegation reference. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(core)) over the profile-defined closed core that carries neither delegation_id nor signature. The delegation object, terminal certificate and single-use CAS token carry only this typed reference; no sibling delegation_digest exists (encoding.md 4.0.1).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7. payload_pattern is the core-registered outer value space the profile MUST stay inside; the profile MAY narrow it further but MUST NOT accept an octet outside it.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32 raw challenge octets together with the challenge consumption ledger row; it is registry-local single-use state, never a federated object ID and never a native UUID column.
special_forms.description: Single-use Organization registration control challenge identifier issued by ak.root.identity.organization_registration.command.prepare.v1. It is registry-allocated, neither content-addressed nor Event-derived, and it never denotes a durable protocol object.

allocation.payload_encoding: 32 octets rendered as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
allocation.uniqueness_rule: The registry MUST atomically reserve the value before returning it and MUST reallocate on any collision with a live or consumed ledger row; a challenge value is never reissued.
allocation.consumption_rule: The registry MUST consume the challenge inside the same transaction that persists (challenge_id, canonical_request_digest, outcome).
allocation.replay_rule: Only a byte-identical retry may return the recorded outcome; the same challenge_id carrying any different canonical_request_digest, or a consumed challenge_id with no matching successful ledger row, MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.
allocation.security_rationale: A caller-chosen or request-derived challenge would let the caller pick freshness and defeat single-use consumption, so the registry mints the full 256-bit value itself and binds the outcome to the exact canonical request bytes.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed OrganizationRegistrationReceipt identifier. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims)), where receipt_claims is exactly the receipt object with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted; it is the same content-addressed family as service_registration_receipt and MUST NOT be reused as a Realm capability, membership, governance-Station designation or service delegation.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque install-plan token; do not parse it as UUIDv7.
special_forms.description: Applet install-plan identifier. The suffix is an opaque non-empty base64url token.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Profile-scoped pseudonymous reference. Each consuming profile defines its own scope boundary and narrows the core-registered outer payload_pattern; it MUST NOT accept an octet outside that space. E2EE credential pseudonyms are Realm-scoped, while push pseudonyms are scoped to the registered recipient service, principal, device, route and salt epoch. Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed ServiceRegistrationReceipt identifier derived from canonical receipt claims. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims)).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete typed content-addressed identifier together with the exact canonical signer-evidence bytes.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed authenticated signer-resolution evidence reference. The suffix is the SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical evidence object under its registered digest rule.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical ak:trust_domain:<scope> value by default. A compressed schema may store the raw scope only in an explicitly named trust_domain_scope column and MUST restore the typed prefix at the persistence boundary.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk root, recovery and authorization proofs. NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kind_registry.uuid_form_rules: The construction is declared per kind by id_form. producer_allocated = RFC 9562 UUIDv7. event_derived = the creating Event's 33-byte token (zero reserved high nibble plus uint4 suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of its digest), canonically encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters and retyped only by replacing the ak:<kind>: prefix. The token requires strict decode plus canonical re-encode validation; regex alone is insufficient.

notification_projection_identity_contrac.notes: The ID is not a signature or read capability. Verify the original source Event and applicable acceptance evidence, bind the complete recipient AccountId, and rederive the ID. Never rewrite the source Event into account_data.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

high_security_session_authentication_pol.public_projection_rule: Without valid sender-constrained proof, an allowlisted operation may return only its contract-defined public metadata projection and MUST NOT grant session or capability semantics. All other ak.self.* operations fail closed.
high_security_session_authentication_pol.new_operation_rule: A new or unknown ak.self.* operation is protected by default; adding an unauthenticated public projection requires explicit registration in this list and a normative operation contract defining that projection.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise registered supported_operation_bundles and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see surface_classes); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>.v1. The kind segment MUST be one of read, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the only safe/idempotent computation kind; its exact GET, QUERY, or POST binding is declared by the operation row according to request shape.
An operation row MUST declare exactly one HTTP binding and MUST NOT declare unregistered method/path aliases.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex read-body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

An operation that invokes current DID authority MUST carry exactly one did_authority object that byte-matches its did-freshness-profile-registry call_sites row. Operations without a real DID-authority call MUST omit it; risk tier never implies DID freshness.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. kind=branched declares a semantic request discriminator plus a closed effect_branches[] list with unique equals values and one final otherwise branch; each branch contains a complete event_log, actor_private_event, or none leaf effect. An event_log branch that is not unconditional MUST additionally name event_submission_path pointing to the caller-signed EventCommitSubmission used by that branch. Field presence is evidence carried by a branch, never the branch discriminator itself. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

Every operation_id is an explicit versioned operation identity ending in .v1. Its stable HTTP endpoint identity is derived by removing the terminal .vN and is used as the OpenAPI operationId; the unversioned identity is not an alias for a versioned operation_id.

Every canonical Arkret HTTP request MUST carry exactly one Arkret-Operation header naming the exact versioned operation_id before body parsing. The receiver MUST verify that the selector is locally advertised and belongs to the selected method/path family and binding. A missing selector fails with operation_selector_required; an empty candidate set, unknown id, duplicate selector, or value outside the route family fails with unsupported_operation_version. Endpoint uniqueness, payload-shape inference, client SDK version, implicit defaults, and version fallback MUST NOT replace the selector. This invariant keeps existing clients stable when another operation version is added to the same HTTP endpoint family.

operation_bundles is the only canonical bundle member source. Each registered bundle freezes one service_kind and a canonical unique set of (operation_id,binding_kind) members; changing a member requires a new bundle id.
Within one service_kind, active current-v1 bundles MUST NOT overlap on an identical (operation_id,binding_kind) pair. Pairs using a different binding kind are distinct.

Only registered ak.operation_bundle.*.v1 ids may appear in current-v1 ServiceDescribe. Current-v1 defines no vendor bundle wire namespace; vendor-private collections may only appear as ignorable x_* metadata and never affect capability decisions. Unknown bundle ids fail closed and are never expanded by name.

Request wire/canonical byte budget violations MUST return payload_too_large (HTTP 413); count-only schema violations with valid request bytes MUST return schema_violation (HTTP 422), except explicit operation count semantics. An otherwise valid request whose complete response or evaluation exceeds its semantic budget returns limit_exceeded (HTTP 413) or its defined typed unavailable result. Request byte errors take precedence over coincident schema errors. Error classification MUST NOT depend on diagnostic text substring matching.

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

delivery_authentication_record.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method and key digest; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id; registration_epoch is the effective destination Applet registration.
delivery_authentication_record.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; its canonical bare did MUST be validated by the registered method adapter and project to both Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id. The effective registration_epoch and actual verification key digest are bound. Direct DID/core-id comparison and did_core_id fragment concatenation are forbidden.
delivery_authentication_record.equality: Receivers recompute sha256(UTF8(digest_domain + newline) || RFC8785_JCS(record)); equal recomputed digests define replay equality. Caller-supplied records or digests are forbidden.

operations.notes: All directions preserve the unique original producer proof and portable signer authorization. Each receiver verifies exact installation aggregate, scope, grant, epoch and native act-on-behalf authority independently. HTTP source signatures and storage receipts do not authorize Events. The Station-to-Applet authoring_context branch carries the accepted Applet Service signer root plus the managed Actor Principal signer root and its exact Station Service attester leaf; the runtime recomputes and atomically persists all three roots before ordinary authoring. Signals retain their independent proof regime.

The Applet service consumes the one signed install_bot or provision_ghost authoring request and returns the exact role-neutral four-Event bundle. All four creation Events use the Applet service as actual producer and reference the same real Service AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence root derived from the accepted registration epoch; a pre-effective Bot or Ghost never signs them. Its durable ledger is keyed by branch subject plus full signed-request digest and preserves exact request/bundle bytes, the Service root, actor key handle, method history, and provision state. No derived request ID or branch-specific Event aliases exist.

durable_effect.rationale: The operation admits no Arkret Event; independently, the Applet service atomically persists the subject/request-digest ledger, exact request and bundle, Applet Service signer root, actor key custody, method history, and provision state before returning

operations.notes: HTTP-only authenticated Station-to-Gateway registration handoff for a Station-approved public Gateway. The HTTP Message Signature binds exact Source-Service-ID, Destination-Service-ID and Content-Digest. The Gateway admits only an explicitly onboarded source Station, partitions storage/log/access by that authenticated source, and accepts notify for the installed registration only from that same Station. Each Station-generated registration_id is immutable: exact replay returns the byte-identical signed durable receipt, different content conflicts, revoked is terminal, and an active successor atomically tombstones its exact supersedes_registration_id. The body and receipt carry no AccountId, principal, Realm or user session. Raw provider route material appears only in the active handoff body and the destination tenant's provider adapter, never in notify, receipt, logs, metrics, traces or cross-tenant indexes.

Provided by the push_gateway role. The source service must be authorized by the exact durable registration. For a trusted public-Gateway installation created by ak.edge.push.command.apply_registration.v1, only the exact source Station that installed it may call notify. Notification devices carry only device_id; registration routes and tokens are not supplied by this request.

Provided only by the authenticated AccountId.station_id Station role. The optional station.push bundle contains both registration operations; a push_gateway role does not acquire Account registration authority.

Provided only by the authenticated AccountId.station_id Station role. The optional station.push bundle contains both registration operations; a push_gateway role does not acquire Account registration authority.

did_authority.purpose: Verify the announce governance proof of the announcing service or organization, and resolve the Station endpoint inside the same first-ingest admission.
Verify the withdraw governance signature of the service or organization that owns the directory entry.

operations.notes: Explicit one-step abandonment with a fresh holder-bound account handoff obtained for this confirmation. Validate exact request_id, principal_id, did_version_id, live lease/fence against the durable onboarding checkpoint and confirm PCR was never accepted. The client displays the fixed consequences before sending. Atomically record one orphan tombstone, suppress the checkpoint and release the lease; exact replay returns the same terminal outcome, while an accepted-PCR race returns identity_creation_already_accepted with zero writes.

The one authenticated step that binds an account-less staged pairing record to an exact AccountId (device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1). The caller is the candidate device itself: it holds the exact device_pairing_request_id and pairing_code, holds the staged candidate key, and authenticates with Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP for a bound pending account handoff. That handoff is the sole source of the exact AccountId, which the candidate signs into device_pairing_target_proof; a server-side side channel or an unsigned request member MUST NOT assert account membership. The Account Authority recomputes the 2.1.2 challenge transcript from its own durable stage, verifies the target signature with the staged new_device_pubkey, requires target_proof.account_id to equal the AccountId this handoff is bound to, and only then moves the record from staged to ready_for_claim. The transition is one-way: ready_for_claim never returns to staged and authorized is never reachable without it. Unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, an expired record and a record that is no longer staged all return an indistinguishable not_found. Exact retry of the same canonical intent returns the same outcome without re-attaching a proof; the same request id with different content conflicts. A successful finalize also supersedes: in the same durable transaction it MUST move every other unaccepted ready_for_claim pending record of that AccountId to terminal expired, keeping the bounded tombstone that preserves exact retry and blocks replay, so the account never holds two approvable records at once. This is what makes the existing MUST NOT in device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1 enforceable, and it is the only way v1 retires the code of an earlier pairing attempt; v1 registers no cancel operation. The supersession key is the AccountId alone, so a refreshed pairing page reusing the same candidate key and a different new device with a fresh candidate key retire the earlier record identically, and adding two new devices in parallel is therefore forbidden. Supersession never authors an Event, grants nothing, and never rewrites the terminal outcome of a record pair_device already accepted; an exact retry performs no second supersession. The durable boundary is the gate-side pending ledger, because only the gate side holds the account binding when the Account Authority is deployed separately from the Station. No Arkret Event is authored and nothing is authorized here.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Station validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether the issuer ledger considers it active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The Account Authority MUST read the same issuer ledger used by issue, refresh, revoke and cascade; lifecycle status distinguishes active, revoked, superseded and dynamically expired records rather than consulting a Principal Event/typed current result. Introspection does not call back to the origin Station and carries no reusable revocation-gate receipt: before accepting each protected self request, that origin Station checks its own exact device/generation pending/RealmCommit state locally in the request transaction. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Station can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. This is the exact-token introspection authority contract: a request-admission introspection MUST use the grant_jwt branch carrying the exact presented token bytes plus the caller's own audience_id, and the resource server MUST NOT locally verify that JWT's signature, replay the issuer DID history, or recompute the issuance preimage, suite-tagged ID or jti. The id branch stays limited to the management/status queries it already served and its active flag MUST NOT authorize a second, not byte-compared JWT. Cached authority results are freshness-bounded projections whose cache key isolates at least the exact token, the expected audience_id and the authority configuration context. Authenticated by the deployment-internal authentication channel registered in zh/sync/service-http-binding.md 2.2.3 (registered principal: the owning Station for that audience); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority-owned controller lifecycle gate an Agent Authority cannot synthesize for itself. Authentication is the deployment-internal contract: it binds the configured caller, the target Station, the trust domain and the allowed operation, and the Account Authority takes the caller identity only from that authenticated relationship. The authenticated source, agent_authority_id and the Station of the controller's complete AccountId MUST be equal and MUST match the authority the principal's current binding names; status and binding values come from the authority's own records, never from a caller-asserted active flag. An unknown principal, a wrong authority or an unauthorized caller all return an unenumerable not_found. The response side is not weakened by the request side being internally authenticated: the attestation signature, the public DID assertion authorization of its verification method, the TTL and exact replay all remain, because the response enters an external Agent evidence chain that the SDK and foreign Stations verify independently. Positive validity MUST NOT exceed 300 seconds.

Issue a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED did to the authenticated service account under stable principal_id. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. Unlike issue_identity_binding_challenge the caller supplies principal_id plus did rather than an unpublished DID operation: the Account Authority MUST resolve did itself at the high freshness tier (synchronous refresh or fail closed), MUST require the registered adapter to project(did)=principal_id, MUST NOT attempt to resolve did_core_id, MUST NOT accept caller-supplied history, and derives did_version_id, log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST additionally require method-native witness / freshness evidence, because accepting registry and Station co-location does not extend trust to third-party DIDs. The <=300s single-use challenge and returned control proof bind account_subject, principal_id, did, holder cnf.jkt, the resolved DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation performs no PCR genesis and reserves no principal: it only proves current control of an existing DID.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id, its canonical operation digest, did_version_id, log_head_digest, and control_key_digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, rate-limits same-holder renewal, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, all derived DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

Issues the replacement device's first Standard grant after a PCR-policy RecoveryTransaction completes. The body carries the terminal device-attested receipt, coordinator attestation, PCR generation and InitialSessionGrantIntent; DID-root evidence is relevant only when that optional factor was enabled. If deployment policy permits reactivation and the original account is deactivated, this operation alone atomically authors the deactivated-to-active successor, restores the same account row, creates the publication outbox entry and issues the first new-generation grant. It never creates a replacement account or second PCR, and it never revives an old session, device or KeyPackage; policy denial or incomplete recovery returns account_deactivated with zero authoritative writes.

Account Authority single-call issuer-ledger SessionGrant issuance with a closed HumanSessionGrantRequest | RecoverySessionGrantRequest | AgentSessionGrantRequest union. OIDC authorization code is never accepted here; authentication-handoffs is the unique code consumer. Returning-human and recovery requests use Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP. Returning-human issuance requires AcceptedDevicePossessionProof and origin revocation-gate allow, consumes the handoff, and emits Standard + complete device_binding. Recovery issuance requires credential_class=recovery_session, binds the account principal/audience, candidate device and handoff DPoP JWK, emits a <=15 minute non-refreshable recovery_candidate_device grant without device_binding, consumes only the request DPoP JTI, and preserves the handoff for recovery completion. Agent issuance keeps its independent agent_key_proof validator. The issuer uses branch-specific request identity and canonical intent to persist one immutable issuance record and signed JWT before responding. Exact replay is byte-identical; conflict and terminal replay fail closed. The client presents every grant only as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP proof. No Principal Event is authored.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The presented grant chain is the stable protocol-sequence identity. The handler validates the ak.session.grant + DPoP when metadata remains, idempotently terminates the Auth-side auth session / complete grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session.v1 when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Exact retries on an already terminal or pruned chain return an equivalent successful no-op; audience mismatch still fails closed. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the presented grant chain is the stable protocol-sequence identity. The Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout.v1 request, then calls this operation over the deployment-internal authentication channel registered in zh/sync/service-http-binding.md 2.2.3 (registered principal: the same deployment's Account Authority) to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's complete grant rotation chain. Exact retries, including an already logged-out, revoked, unknown or pruned chain, return an equivalent successful terminal outcome without a second side effect. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout.v1. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

One controller-signed authorize Event with inline Ed25519 public_key, exact supersedes and private scope disclosure binds a frozen candidate by pairing_request_id and approval_request_id. The verifier reads its authoritative frozen record (or authenticated verifier-only agent view), independently verifies PoP and candidate, and persists the exact command. Same-candidate PoP refresh does not invalidate approval. Accepted RealmCommit processing automatically activates after rechecking current handle, expiry, candidate, parent authority and activation fence; cancellation or changed authority is terminal. Exact retry returns/reconciles the durable outcome and never revives authority.

Durable terminal exact replay is keyed by pairing request id, approving AccountId/device and canonical request digest. It returns the same accepted result without a second Event or stage consumption; same identity with changed intent conflicts.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger SessionGrant rotation with a closed HumanSessionGrantRefreshRequest | AgentSessionGrantRefreshRequest union. Both branches present the predecessor as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof and carry no client-generated challenge or generic proof_kind. Human refresh additionally carries AcceptedDevicePossessionProof purpose=session_grant_refresh; the origin verifies it under the locked current accepted-device key and applies the predecessor signed device_binding as expected binding in the same current-authorization linearization. Agent refresh carries only AgentSessionRefreshProof and revalidates current runtime-key authorization/lifecycle through its independent validator. The stable request identity is (predecessor_grant_id, refresh_request_digest). One issuer transaction creates the active successor with a fresh issuance nonce, preserves subject/scope/audience/cnf.jkt/session_id, and atomically supersedes the predecessor. Exact replay returns the recorded successor; conflicting or terminal replay never issues another. Account/passkey restoration uses a fresh AccountHandoff then issue, and PCR recovery uses its dedicated completion operation; neither is a refresh proof kind. No Principal Event is authored.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. The body selects exactly one branch: an already-published DID control proof, or account-first identity_creation. Both branches submit outer did and principal_id; every repeated did/principal_id in the selected proof, identity-creation object and PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte. The Account Authority independently validates the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=principal_id. The published-DID proof branch uses the durable challenge pins and creates no identity-creation lease or PCR genesis. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST additionally present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] of the entry pinned by did_version_id (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod), requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly, and requires its canonical multikey SHA-256 to equal control_key_digest. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, derives pcr_realm_id only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id, and writes the service-account binding. Account-first PCR genesis persists the same verified did, method_history_head and version_id in initial_resolution. Every success returns a signed binding_receipt that binds binding_kind, principal_id, did, did_version_id and control_key_digest; identity_creation_lease_id and lease_fence appear only for binding_kind=identity_creation. The (account, principal_id, registration_anchor_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Beyond authoring the genesis Events this operation publishes a public did:webvh log entry and commits a one-account-one-principal binding that can never be rebound. Retry and audit logic MUST treat it as cross-service irreversible even though the closed durable_effect kind vocabulary can only name the Event-log half.

operations.notes: The only client entry point for self-initiated account erasure (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). The Account Authority accepts it directly on the gate surface: it authenticates the holder as a high-risk action, durably records the erasure intent and continues its existing erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord issuance flow within the same service — there is no cross-service handoff, because the record issuer, the status-transition legality oracle and the section-8 fanout orchestrator are all the Account Authority, so no 'accepted but issuance pending on another service' intermediate state exists. Authentication freshness is judged locally by the Account Authority, the only party holding recent login / WebAuthn / recovery key facts; a Station MUST NOT determine or approximate it from session-grant introspection or local session state (introspection deliberately projects neither auth_time nor proof kind). The success response is an acceptance confirmation only: the current status is observed through the existing account-status read surface and physical completion only through the erasure receipt rail. The Account Authority MAY insert a deployment-governed withdrawal window (possibly zero) between acceptance and record signing, echoing withdrawal_window_ends_at when one exists; once the erasure_pending record is signed the request is irreversible and any withdrawal MUST fail closed. Replaying the same request_id returns the recorded acceptance outcome; the same request_id with different canonical bytes is duplicate_conflict with zero writes; a different request_id while a live unsigned-record intent exists is failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending. A session that does not satisfy the deployment's fresh high-risk action authentication policy is rejected with reauthentication_required.

Durable issuer-ledger session revocation. The stable request identity binds issuer, operation kind, authenticated principal/session, canonical target selector and canonical request digest. One issuer transaction records the exact outcome and idempotently transitions matching active records to revoked. Same identity and canonical intent replays the byte-identical recorded outcome after current caller authorization is revalidated; the same identity with different intent is duplicate_conflict with zero additional state changes. Introspection is not a substitute for resolving an uncertain mutation outcome.

Unique current-v1 OIDC authorization-code consumer. Account Authority exchanges and validates the code and issues an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key plus the deployment-local stable account_subject. The external callback receiver that owns the redirect transaction validates state; Account Authority validates state only when it owns that transaction, and always validates issuer, token exchange/PKCE, redirect_uri and ID Token nonce. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, issue_did_binding_challenge, issue_identity_abandonment_challenge, abandon_identity_creation, register, issue_session_grant, and issue_recovery_completion_grant. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy. Bound clients normalize local evidence before choosing returning issue, pairing-first Device Setup or diagnostics; identity onboarding accepts only the other two states. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. When deployment policy allows reactivation, fresh account authentication may return a bound recovery-candidate handoff for the original deactivated account, but the handoff does not change status and ordinary register, issue and refresh remain blocked; only recovery completion may reactivate it. Policy denial returns account_deactivated with zero recovery writes.

Authenticated retrieval of one pending pairing request by its normalized eight-character code, so a desktop browser with no camera can join a device by typing the code shown on the new device (device-lifecycle.md 2.1.1). The caller is a current accepted, non-pending-revocation device of an exact AccountId and the code is the whole input; it MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. The service returns the resolved bootstrap and the byte-equivalent target proof only when the code hits a unique unexpired ready_for_claim unconsumed request whose signed account_id and gate audience equal the caller's own account, and when proof, staged key, request id, code and transcript digest all agree. Unknown, wrong, expired, superseded, cross-account, not yet finalized and already consumed codes MUST all return the same not_found, so an error shape never says whether a code exists or which account it belongs to. The response carries no private key, no session credential, no recovery material and nothing about any other device of the account. Claiming retrieves a request and grants nothing: the accepted device still has to review it and sign ak.device.authorize. Calls are rate limited per caller device, per AccountId and per service, and a request locks out after its cumulative failure budget.

Read-only DPoP-bound projection of the current Account Authority identity-creation lease or established binding. The response is rebuilt from durable server state on every call and accepts no client-authored phase, goal, checkpoint, or recovery material. Clients use it to reconcile local onboarding artifacts after reload, callback, process restart, or an uncertain command result.

Runtime submits one candidate with an Ed25519 PoP over the authoritative handle, at-least-128-bit pairing secret, service DID, stable raw-key binding and at-most-five-minute window. Same-binding retries refresh the verified PoP while preserving candidate/approval/notification identity; different candidate on one handle conflicts. Controller signs the inline-key authorize Event once; approval is independent of PoP refresh. Secret and proof occur only in request body and confidential verifier material.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries the authorized key binding plus current_signer_evidence and signer_resolution_evidence_ref. The runtime compares authorized_public_key_digest against its own key, independently verifies and rebuilds the signer evidence/ref, persists that closure, and then authors Events offline; authorized_event_ref never substitutes for signer_resolution_evidence_ref. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state staged. The pairing_code MUST be unique across the whole live pending set of the service, because it is also the sole lookup key of the authenticated code claim; a user-driven refresh is simply another call to this operation and mints a distinct request and code; the earlier record is closed not here but by the next successful finalize for that AccountId, and a record still in staged is harmless because resolve, code claim and pair_device all require ready_for_claim. The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving device only over the out-of-band channel, so this anonymous surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint, and a mirrored copy could never be authoritative anyway. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing: the account binding happens one step later, at the authenticated ak.gate.account.command.finalize_device_pairing.v1. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: it does not carry the challenge proof, the target attestation, or the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs, and those MUST NOT be mirrored here. Only a record that has already been finalized to ready_for_claim can be resolved; resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a record that is not ready_for_claim so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device that has independently verified the out-of-band challenge proof and target attestation before driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state staged before finalize and ready_for_claim after it; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. A record superseded by a later successful ak.gate.account.command.finalize_device_pairing.v1 for the same AccountId reports the same expired during that retention period and is indistinguishable from a naturally elapsed TTL; the query credential is the request id plus the pairing code, so only the candidate device that minted the record can observe it and no prior existence is disclosed. authorized_event_ref is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in device-lifecycle.md §5.4.1: the target device MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key_did / hpke_key / algorithms and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally, and MUST fail closed and warn the user otherwise.

Reads the current public principal resolution projection from the known Station. The response carries only the account pair, the projection, bounded adapter method evidence and the Station projection attestation; it MUST NOT carry principal_control_realm_id, PCR genesis Event, genesis receipt, resolution Events or accepted RealmCommit. Account-internal audit material moved to ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1, so this surface has no history selector. This is a second-hop projection fetch, not a global resolver or authorization oracle. Sensitive consumers fetch fresh, verify the attestation proof under the current station_id method history, independently run the registered DID method adapter, and require project(did)=principal_id; durable storage of arbitrary remote-principal bindings is not required.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.

The caller MUST author and sign the exact ak.consent.grant (decision=accept) or ak.consent.revoke (decision=deny or revoke) EventCommitSubmission. The facade verifies the detached operation signature and the Event authority/correlation, then submits the Event unchanged through authority Event submission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign consent state. A revoke with no matching active observed dots is rejected without disclosing holder state. Exact Event replay returns the same accepted Event reference.

discriminator.description: The caller-declared semantic MIMI update kind. The decoded opaque payload MUST carry the same kind before a branch is admitted.

operations.notes: Return a nonce-bound genesis-to-current authority chain; locators are hints and never authority.

Returns current AuthenticatedServiceResolution containing service_id, service_kind, complete method_history_evidence and normalized_did_document. Consumers independently verify method-native history, current state, service identity/type, unique canonical HTTPS DID service endpoint and second-hop describe binding. Durable native method state prevents rollback and fork; cache TTL is at most 300 seconds and failed freshness checks never extend it. Endpoint refresh does not require Realm rebind; a changed service core requires a new authorized binding.

Back-binding activation of one provisioned private record to exactly one accepted ak.invite.third_party (third-party-invites.md section 7.5). The body carries provisioning_id and the Station-signed ThirdPartyInviteAcceptanceAttestation; the attestation is the whole authorization, so a caller-reported invite id, a caller-computed invite digest, an Event signature or an HTTP success MUST NOT be accepted in its place. The service verifies the Station service identity and signature, audience, exact verification_id, the attestation's signed expires_at/invite_expires_at bounds, and member-for-member equality of author, Realm, expiry and public material against the frozen provisioning record, recomputes invite_digest from the attested typed current result per section 4.2, then atomically persists the unique binding and the delivery intent. One provisioning record binds to one invite forever: a second attestation naming a different invite, Realm or author is refused and never rebinds, rotates the key or reissues the token. A byte-identical retry, a concurrent duplicate and a retry after a restart all return the original binding.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Delivery to an external mail or SMS gateway cannot be recalled. The intent MUST be durable before success is returned, and the delivered material stays the one invite this activation bound; stopping an already delivered invite requires an authorized writer's ak.invite.revoke.

operations.notes: Token presentation surface of the 3PID invite verification service (third-party-invites.md section 4.1). The invitee's client submits invite_token, realm_id, subject_account_id, subject_did and a client claim_nonce in the JSON body; the service validates token, expiry, claim count and Realm binding, atomically consumes the token, signs the ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1 transcript with the invite's verification_public_key and returns invite_id, token_commitment and binding_proof. invite_token in the URL query string or path segment is rejected with third_party_invite_token_in_query and the token SHOULD be invalidated; a knock_restricted Realm is rejected with unsupported_join_rule; every other failure is non-enumerable (section 6). A consumed token MUST NOT be re-bound to a different subject; the same (realm_id, subject_account_id, claim_nonce) MAY be answered with the same binding_proof inside the recoverable window (section 6.1).

Private-material provisioning entry of the 3PID invite verification service (third-party-invites.md section 7.2). An authenticated inviter submits request_id, realm_id, inviter_account_id, verification_id, oob_code_kind, the private mailto:/tel: delivery target and the requested expiry, signed under ak.third_party_invite_provision_request_proof.v1 with the service DID as audience. The service mints and durably keeps the token, the per-invite 256-bit token_salt or lookup pepper and the per-invite ephemeral signing key, then returns only the public third_party_invite object, the effective expires_at, the activation deadline and an opaque provisioning_id. It MUST NOT return the token, salt, pepper, ephemeral private key or the delivery target, MUST NOT create a pending Realm Invite, MUST NOT mint an invite_id and MUST NOT deliver anything before activation. Same request_id plus byte-identical canonical intent replays the original outcome; same request_id plus different intent is duplicate_conflict with no second set of material. An unimplemented oob_code_kind or delivery scheme is unsupported_feature; every existence failure stays non-enumerable (section 6).

Lifecycle and out-of-band delivery position of one provisioning record (third-party-invites.md section 7.6). provisioning_id is the whole query credential and MUST travel only in the JSON body. It is the recovery surface after a lost provisioning or activation response and the only standard delivery observation point. The outcome carries provisioning_state, and once activated also invite_id, activated_at, delivery_state and delivery_attempt_count; it MUST NOT carry the token, salt, pepper, ephemeral private key, delivery target or any 3PID-derived value, and MUST NOT reveal whether the invitee opened the invite. An unknown handle, a handle belonging to another inviter and a deleted record MUST be indistinguishable.

Replicates one exact Account Authority-signed AccountStatusRecord. The receiver verifies transport authentication, record identity/proof, exact account/principal/binding tuple, sequence continuity and previous_account_status_record_id, then atomically advances its monotonic replica and emits a signed receipt. A gap returns dependency_missing with zero writes; stale, duplicate and fork are distinguished without rebuilding or re-signing the record. For status=erasure_pending, accepted or duplicate is returned only after a durable physical-erasure intent keyed by receiver service, account, triggering record and storage boundary exists. Same Idempotency-Key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: The signed record is the only erasure command. Acceptance is forbidden until the receiver has a durable execution intent; physical completion is established only by a verified ErasureReceiptPackage.

operations.notes: Service-authenticated bounded read of a contiguous Account Authority issuer-ledger range for freshness and replica gap recovery. The Account Authority returns original signed records in status_seq order and never exposes an account to a service without an existing exact account/principal relationship. Empty, unknown and unauthorized are non-enumerating at the operation boundary.

Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, or bilateral continuity-checkpoint control. Authorizing source receipts, directional proofs and the receipted outbox exist only after the exact source command unit is RealmCommit-committed and its effects atomically installed. The receiver verifies the independently derived source Station's historical service attestation and original holder producer separately; no private PCR bootstrap or generic authority-commit proof disclosure is added, and source_checkpoint is not a RealmCommit. The continuity branch carries a one-sided proposal; the receiver recomputes the exact core, verifies the proposer signature, appends only its own participant service-authority signature, durably commits the complete checkpoint and returns it with a signed control receipt. Exact replay returns the same bytes; same-sequence different-digest forks fail closed. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events. The original source-signed Event receipt or lineage includes the exact producer_signer method and Ed25519 raw32 key. This permits the first Contact carrier without an existing relationship or private PCR disclosure; it is an exact-Event producer projection, not reusable Control or device authority. The source-signed producer projection uses a closed delegated branch with delegated_actor_did exactly for legal Agent controller-device Events containing executed_by; human and Agent-runtime branches forbid it. This complete Agent public DID locator is frozen from verified native identity, rechecked against the exact Actor/controller/Station, and grants no authority.

Authenticated Account-Authority-to-origin-Station current-device and revocation gate. Deployment-internal only: the registered Account-Authority-to-owning-Station relationship is authenticated by the channel contract in zh/sync/service-http-binding.md 2.2.3, which is the whole authentication contract and replaces the default service-to-service signature. The decision receipt carries neither proof nor verification_method; its authenticity and integrity come from that channel, a receipt that did not arrive over it MUST be rejected, and there is no external calling branch. returning_session_grant_issue and human session_grant_refresh bind AcceptedDevicePossessionProof; registration/recovery session_grant_issue uses its separately verified durable evidence and forbids this proof. Under one device lock/serializable transaction the origin reads the durable current accepted-device projection, verifies any required proof with its key, derives authorization Event/generation, evaluates pending/revoked state and persists the durable decision record binding proof digest and intent. A lock-external key/status read followed by a second gate transaction is forbidden. expected selectors are required for refresh and may be omitted for both issue action classes. Only allow carries derived selectors and can produce complete human device_binding; authority_mismatch maps to device_unauthorized and every non-allow yields zero grant. Exact replay returns the byte-identical <=30 second receipt.

Service-authenticated terminal erasure-result fanout only; it never requests or triggers deletion. Source-Service-ID MUST equal receipt.issuer. The receiver verifies the closed trigger union, receipt, issuer authority, every proof, receipt_digest and exact retained-stub binding before durable acceptance. Same key and canonical body returns the byte-identical signed acceptance; different body returns duplicate_conflict with zero writes. Account erasure requires the account_status_record trigger branch to equal the accepted erasure_pending record; other erasure uses the event branch.

Service-authenticated exact receipt-package lookup for the issuer, receiver or an explicitly authorized auditor. It is non-enumerating: unauthorized, unknown and hidden receipt identifiers produce the same not_found response.
