The returned retained stub is the exact object accepted with the receipt and MUST NOT be reconstructed from later state.
Forward an exact producer Event to the verified current governance Station; a non-authority peer cannot accept it locally.

Directory-only exact resolve: authenticate the Directory, revalidate its source-signed DirectorySourceRefAccess, and resolve only byte-identical Event/Commit/stream/position refs contained by that carrier; no scan or caller-supplied Event is accepted as proof.
Replicate one visibility-authorized stream from its current governance Station.

Private Station to Station invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.account_id.station_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee_account_id equals invite_address.account_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Atomic cross-Station KeyPackage claim. The destination Station is the sole atomic claim-ledger authority for its KeyPackage inventory. The authenticated source Station first validates the participant request against its exact local account/device/generation durable state; revocation_pending fails before any remote call or inventory disclosure and is exposed only as the existing opaque claim_failed result. Request and response carry no PCR/control-history or separate signer-evidence sidecar. Every claim binds the matching accepted authorization Event id, whose unique producer proof and signer evidence must validate when independently replayed, plus the signed destination claim receipt, exact selectors and KeyPackage signature. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and the canonical request digest.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.

Station-to-Station device directory and published prekey-bundle read, the only registered carrier for a cross-Station keys/query target. requester_account_id.station_id equals the authenticated Source-Service-ID and every target account_id.station_id equals the Destination-Service-ID; no client SessionGrant, DPoP or local bearer is ever forwarded and clients never call this surface. The destination completes transport authentication before any target read, then re-derives the declared relationship from its own accepted state: realm_membership requires both parties to be current effective joined members of that exact Realm, while contact reads only the target's own current outbound Contact scope and never requires a shared Realm. Purpose is authorized independently. Absent, invisible, unrelated, revoked, fenced and policy-denied targets collapse into an omitted row or device_result_unavailable, rate limited per requester and per target. Rows carry the origin's own attestation and signer evidence ref; the destination adds no response signature. Request <=64 KiB with 1..16 accounts and 32 devices each; complete response <=512 KiB, no continuation. Cross-Station single-use material remains the MLS KeyPackage claim contract.

Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every echoed scope/group/epoch/ref/digest selector, hashes raw bytes against both explicit digests and content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before returning an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Account Authority transparently relays the exact client-signed PCR genesis unit after authenticating the service account and freezing the account/principal reservation. The outer service signature is transport authentication only. Principal admission independently validates the DID inception root, identity_creation_control_proof, the event-derived PCR id retype(create.event_id) which is never derived from the principal DID or subject and is never server-chosen, empty checkpoint, ordered root-signed create plus founding-device-signed authorize, single-direction payload digest binding, lease fence and expiry. Acceptance is atomic and create-once at the account dimension: two genesis attempts produce two different realm_id values, so implementations MUST NOT detect concurrency by id equality. Exact replay returns the original pcr_genesis_unit receipt and a conflicting unit performs zero writes.
Install a planned dual-signed authority handoff after complete snapshot and all stream heads are imported.

Restricted outcome of exactly one forwarded join application, read by the applicant's own Station before that account is a member. The holder Station verifies service-to-service authentication, that applicant_account_id.station_id equals the Source-Service-ID, that it is the Destination-Service-ID, and that event_id is the exact Event this source forwarded for this applicant. received carries no decision; the other five states carry the durable event_commit_submission_decision_read_outcome for the same proposal and their proposal_state MUST agree. Unknown Realm, unknown Event, wrong source and an application belonging to another account share one non-enumerating not_found. The read discloses nothing beyond this application and never becomes a general governance, roster or proposal listing surface.

Initial closed join intent or opaque continuation cursor; freeze the unique confirmed Realm head and exact request identity, recheck intent and each object scope disclosure authorization on every page/replay. Typed RealmCommit/Event/governance dependency/applicant predecessor pages; full independent replay before authoring. Required but undisclosable private-scope material fails with revision_unavailable. An invite grants no private Circle read authority. 8 MiB per page, never a total history cap.

Pre-join preview of one directed invite, read by the invitee's own Station from the exact inviter Station named by inviter_account_id.station_id. The caller uses service-to-service authentication and never forwards the invitee's local bearer or session credential; requester_account_id.station_id MUST equal the authenticated Source-Service-ID and the holder MUST be the Destination-Service-ID. The holder resolves the exact invite in its accepted state, checks the invite binds that complete invitee AccountId, is unexpired and unrevoked, and discloses only what the effective ak.realm.preview_policy permits for the invited audience. join_candidates, source_refs, stale and divergent are Directory-result provenance and MUST be omitted. A valid invite whose policy discloses nothing returns the minimal bound preview; unknown Realm, unknown or mismatched invite, wrong source, revoked or expired credential and an absent preview policy share one non-enumerating not_found under a fixed timing bucket. The outcome is not membership and never carries the invite token back.
Transient encrypted Signal rail. It creates no durable Event or RealmCommit, does not advance any authority stream, and grants no delivery or authorization proof.

The wrapper carries one DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Establish the local binding for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id plus the current published did; the receiver independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The referenced challenge MUST bind both identifiers, local_admin_subject and the requested scope set, and the method-native control transcript MUST bind organization_id, did, the pinned version_id/log_head_digest and that challenge context. The outcome and signed receipt echo both identifiers; the receipt also binds version_id and control_key_digest so the accepted control state remains auditable. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. Idempotency is per generation: replaying the current generation's byte-identical request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. This operation registers a reference and local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, make this deployment the controller, or create Realm, membership, governance-Station authority, capability or service delegation.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; before issuing the challenge the registry independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The response challenge echoes and binds both identifiers together with purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, requested scopes, beneficiary local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds. Two phases are mandatory: the registry remembers this challenge, then ensure supplies a method-native proof over the same control transcript. Folding the challenge into ensure would let the caller supply its own, defeating freshness and single use. The challenge MUST be consumed on first successful use. Deliberately not idempotent: every call mints a fresh nonce, and the caller MUST prove against the newest challenge.

Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt, returning created=false. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published did; the receiver independently resolves and validates did with the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=organization_id. The fresh challenge and method-native control transcript bind both identifiers plus the refreshed version_id/log_head_digest. The refreshed outcome and signed receipt echo organization_id and did and bind version_id and control_key_digest. A same-core did refresh updates resolution/control state, not identity. Scopes are not renegotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control after controller rotation and a first-time proof must not authorise the relationship indefinitely.

Withdraw the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id only, returning the current binding outcome with a receipt whose status=revoked and created=false. No did is required because revoke addresses the already-bound local identity rather than resolving or proving fresh external control. This local act does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history. revoked is terminal for the generation; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure with did, a new challenge and a new control proof.

Read the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id without creating or mutating state; returns created=false. The outcome includes the current published did and signed receipt, with project(did)=organization_id and receipt/control-state bindings defined by OrganizationRegistrationOutcome and OrganizationRegistrationReceipt. Only bindings the caller is authorised to manage or see are returned. A caller with no such authorisation MUST receive the same not-found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the query cannot enumerate which organizations a deployment has bound.

The configured Account Station provides verified public identity resolution to its clients through this standard operation. Clients bind the exact DID/subject/purpose to their trusted Station context without fetching method history. A server or independent verifier admitting external resolver material validates the native method evidence and historical authority; remote self-assertions are not trusted. Registration before an Account session requires the expected authenticated registration service/issuer binding. Requested evidence must be derived from verified state or fail closed.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation as a Principal Control Realm ak.policy.set EventCommitSubmission. The canonical Event payload is {policy_id,value}; value is the complete RecoveryPolicy, both policy ids MUST match, and state/reason MUST be absent. Event actor/scope, value.principal_id, lease and accepted control RealmCommit MUST agree. The command returns success only after the Event is covered by the immutable acceptance_basis; before RealmCommit materialization it returns retry-safe revision_unavailable for the same Event id.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Creates one durable recovery session owned by the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt presented as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP. request_id, canonical create intent, candidate device, principal, audience and grant coordinates are immutable. Same request identity plus identical intent returns the retained session; a different intent or reuse of one grant for another session fails duplicate_conflict.

did_authority.when: proof_kind == did_root and the accepted PCR recovery policy explicitly enables the factor

operations.notes: Requires the exact recovery_session grant id and cnf.jkt frozen by create. Proof transcript binds request_id, grant id, cnf.jkt and the complete recovery session tuple. Exact proof replay returns the retained verified outcome; another proof intent after terminal transition fails closed.

Idempotently return or create the service identity bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) registration key. The client supplies did plus the client-controlled signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof, requires state.id=did, projects did to the returned service_id did_core_id, and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base_url) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) key without creating or mutating identity state.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Carries exactly one holder-signed profile_event EventCommitSubmission and no unsigned patch. event.realm_id is the exact account-local PCR Realm selector; accepted-profile presence is evaluated only in that PCR lineage. If it has no accepted Actor Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.create; its actor_profile ID is derived by retyping the create Event ID and payload.object must omit id. If it has an accepted Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.update, payload.target_ref must equal that create-derived ID, and the signed patch remains limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref and profile_fields.<key>. Both branches bind realm scope to the same PCR and event.actor_id to the session principal. On create payload.object.principal_id must equal that principal; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id must equal it. Direct holder proof is required without executor or Applet provenance. Event preconditions are empty; update concurrency uses only optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service forwards the exact bytes through authority Event submission without authoring, rebuilding, co-signing, choosing an ID or adding a concurrency guard. Profile writes are ordinary data. Successful durable independent admission returns the outcome without RealmCommit coverage or advancement; exact retry returns the stored byte-identical outcome. The single accepted effect advances the holder account-aggregate projection once; it creates no Directory announcement or account-data Event.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. Because the operation has no account-local-lineage selector, profile is present only when exactly one accepted profile is unambiguous across the principal's PCR lineages; multiple accepted lineages fail closed by omitting profile, never by choosing an implicit current PCR. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Bounded account long polling with independently paged Realm summaries, at most 16 selected Realm details, segmented global baselines, explicit filter replacement and durable cursor recovery. Empty Realm selection returns no detail. Current authorization and invalidation channels are never window-filtered. Canonical frame <=8 MiB; a round <=16 MiB and <=16 frames; see client-sync section 2.3. HTTP filter and realm_list each use one percent-encoded RFC 8785 JSON query value, preserving empty objects/arrays; dotted/deepObject aliases are not accepted. notifications.items is one closed union discriminated by id form: ak:notification:<uuidv7> is the Agent runtime approval branch and ak:notification_projection:<token> is the ordinary source-Event current row, sharing one projection position, one notifications baseline channel and the same per-frame budget. Ordinary rows carry no inbox state and are re-authorized on every frame, frozen baseline pages included; there is no second notification list operation. See client-sync section 3.1.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.

Submits the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event. The actor-private typed current result subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so only the holder may sign it and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. expected_revision is the Event payload's; it is no longer a query parameter. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused here.

Reads one account_data entry by account_data_key key, including its compare-and-set revision. Returns not_found when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; the not_found error.details carry account_data_cas_conflict_details so the caller still learns current_revision.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write as a compare-and-set whole-value replacement: expected_revision must equal the accepted revision (0 to create) and the stored revision becomes expected_revision + 1. A mismatch returns cas_conflict with account_data_cas_conflict_details and stores nothing, so a stale offline retry can never overwrite a newer write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.

Only outward carrier for the PCR-resident ak.profile.create / ak.profile.update facts. A global profile Event lives in its owner's Principal Control Realm, so a co-member cannot reach it through a Realm-scoped read and MUST NOT reach it through a cross-principal actor selector on ak.self.events.read.scan.v1. Authorization is current effective joined membership of body realm_id for both the caller and each returned actor; realm_id MUST NOT be a Principal Control Realm. Each row returns the display projection and one exact signed profile Event as provenance. No covering RealmCommit exists for these ordinary writes. The authenticated own-Station projection is not an independently proven complete CRDT state; a patch Event alone cannot reconstruct the full profile. It grants no authority and exposes no other PCR Event. Unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, non-member actor and unauthorized caller all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot probe membership or account existence.

Controller-only full replacement of one Account-Authority-owned per-scope selection. The authenticated bearer+DPoP session is the authority proof. First write uses expected_version=0; each accepted write increments the exact agent/scope slot by one. Governance ceilings and ordinary Agent capabilities are evaluated at action time and are not copied into this record.

Authenticated controller view. The Station that owns the pairing candidate is the single owner of the raw PoP material and verifies it there; the Account Authority consumes the authenticated exact outcome and does not read verifier-only raw material through this operation. No generic account impersonation or caller-selected candidate is allowed.

Prepare fixes the new|existing branch, every reducer-derived coordinate, Event ID, canonical unsigned Event bytes and digest. It returns two controller-signing drafts for a new Sidecar and only an attach draft for an existing Sidecar. Commit accepts only proofs appended to those exact drafts. First ensure atomically admits exactly [ak.sidecar.create, ak.sidecar.context.attach]; attach must reference the reserved create Event with role after. The parent-Realm bootstrap exception is scoped only to create.

Controller-only paginated Sidecar list, optionally filtered by realm_id. Returns only Sidecars owned by the authenticated controller and never ordinary Circles or another controller's existence stubs.

Controller-only dedicated Sidecar read surface. Returns the typed Sidecar plus read-only owned/effective Agent sets, native MLS context and reconciliation readiness. Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope.

The four creation Events carry one real Applet Service signer-evidence ref. The successful transaction durably retains that exact Service root with the Event set and install state. Once the managed Actor resolution projection is accepted, completion atomically materializes and retains its Principal root plus the exact Station Service attester leaf and enqueues the existing authoring_context delivery; runtime signer inputs are not mirrored into the administrator outcome.

The active Applet service submits only Realm, exact external tuple, and optional display input. The Station derives every current registration, grant, registration-epoch, package, hosting, and time coordinate, atomically supersedes any prior uncommitted generation for the same branch subject, and returns the exact persisted signed authoring request.

durable_effect.rationale: No Event is admitted, but the Station durably records the current subject generation and exact signed request before returning

operations.notes: All four creation Events use the Applet Service as actual producer and carry its real Service signer-evidence ref; the pre-effective Ghost never signs this unit. Commit durably retains that root with the four Events and Ghost state. Completion atomically materializes the Ghost Principal root and exact Station Service attester leaf and enqueues the existing authoring_context delivery; the synchronous outcome does not mirror runtime signer inputs.

durable_effect.rationale: No Event is admitted, but the Station atomically persists the branch-subject winner, exact unsigned payload, exact signed request, and superseded generations before returning

operations.notes: Query parameters are realm_id, optional subject_actor_id and optional at. subject_actor_id is a percent-encoded canonical JSON ActorId, including Account and Service branches. Omission selects the authenticated credential's exact ActorId. subject_actor_id is the only accepted subject parameter, so subject, subject_station_id and subject_account_id are invalid; no principal-only, local-service, bearer-service, DID-document or inferred-routing fallback is allowed.

Optional query realm_id and cursor. Explicit subject and subject_station_id MUST be paired did_core_id values identifying an exact AccountId. Omitting both selects only the authenticated credential's exact AccountId. Handles, principal-only requests and inferred Station fallbacks are forbidden; self authorization compares the entire AccountId.

Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend kinds (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is backend-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event carried in create_event through authority Event submission; the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service MUST NOT mint it, and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_id, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; the Circle scope stays plaintext until its own ak.mls.genesis is accepted.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through authority Event submission; payload.circle_id MUST equal the path circle_id and the complete target ActorId is payload.member_id. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor add a capability verdict to the closed payload.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through authority Event submission. Path actor_id is one percent-encoded canonical JSON ActorId segment, not a bare principal DID; it is a route selector and does not rename the Event field. The Event membership MUST be leave and payload.expected_membership MUST carry the concrete current membership as its signed expected_revision guard; payload.circle_id MUST equal its path identifier and payload.member_id MUST equal the entire decoded path ActorId, including Station and branch. event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Event carried in grant_event through authority Event submission. payload.consent_id is the producer-allocated typed current result subject and the security-set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>', so the service chooses neither and MUST NOT synthesize the Event. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (the exact current authority-root controller; root_control_only forbids independent controller/Agent delegation).

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_principal_id defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent typed current result. On admission the recipient Station writes one holder-private ak.account.holder_quarantine entry with surface_kind consent_request, carrying no Event ref and none of the invite_delivery branch members; it shares the invite delivery quota, ledger and CAS chokepoint. Because this operation declares no idempotency key and carries no nonce, that branch deduplicates by live-entry uniqueness over (account_id, source_peer_principal_id, consent_scope). The written entry is holder-private service-local material, so durable_effect stays none.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Event carried in revoke_event through authority Event submission. Its payload.revoked_event_refs MUST enumerate the active grant dots being removed for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope), read back from consent_view.active_grant_dots. Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes and MUST still enumerate every dot; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Lists holder-private consent typed results for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive typed current result state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent typed current result selected by the required peer query parameter. The authenticated actor determines the holder coordinate; peers never receive this DTO.

Holder-authorized deterministic compaction of the oldest contiguous terminal Contact prefix. The server computes the core from accepted history; callers cannot submit or choose it. Cross-service pairs use the continuity_checkpoint branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit.v1: the receiver recomputes, countersigns, durably commits and returns the complete checkpoint in one round trip, then the proposer commits the exact returned bytes. Exact replay returns the same checkpoint; same sequence with another digest is continuity_invalid and has no winner. Export reuses continuity_evidence on ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 and import reuses the Contact request continuity_evidence field.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted. Recontact may import one generic mutually signed bilateral prefix checkpoint plus at most 64 uncompressed tail rounds. Missing material is continuity_evidence_unavailable; invalid, rollback or forked material is continuity_invalid. The same trust domain and exact ActorId pair cannot reset its lineage or founding slot. Missing continuity must be recovered or explicitly imported; a full tail without a bilateral checkpoint stays blocked. Only an explicitly initiated first contact for a legally different exact ActorId pair creates an independent root, without inherited checkpoint, history, audit identity, DM or MLS state.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject.v1 operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact round and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Authenticated holder projection from server-verified durable Contact evidence. pending_incoming includes request_event_ref and the exact optional request_message; respond/reject use peer and request_event_ref. Complete continuity_evidence is exported only for explicit boolean query include_continuity=true (default false); online recontact uses Station durable checkpoint and bounded tail. Private Consent and account-data notes are not Contact authority.

Authenticated exact AccountId selects its unique accepted PCR and current PrincipalResolutionProjection, independent of optional profile. Before the first accepted RealmCommit, only the exact atomically accepted genesis current is eligible while no accepted resolution successor exists; derived cache metadata is not authority. The own Station validates method history; no portable evidence or observation time is returned. Wrong or invisible account returns not_found; unresolved verified current state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. The sender's exact durable device/generation state is checked in the queue transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and enqueues nothing. Each target carries a sender-assigned device_message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_account_id, sender_device_id, device_message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates. An encrypted DC has one immutable scope-derived MLS group and monotonic epoch lineage; the response carries exact current group_state_ref. Repair is an ordinary Commit in that group. If all private group state is lost, the old DC Realm is terminal and a new conversation requires a new Realm id. No second group, epoch reset or timeout takeover exists. Found MUST include coordinates.binding_event_ref naming an accepted endorsement for authoring. Clients trust their own Station current result and exact committed proposal decision; they do not replay a governance history closure.
Submit an exact producer Event to its current Realm governance Station. The Account Station reports committed only after receiving RealmCommit.
Read one authorized Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream by continuous stream_position.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Authorized account-internal resolution audit evidence: PCR realm id, genesis Event and receipt, current and bounded predecessor resolution Events, and an accepted RealmCommit covering the disclosed state. Authorization is only a current holder session bound to the exact account_id; recovery first completes the existing recovery transaction and becomes the current holder rather than introducing a second audit authorization path. Unknown account, wrong AccountId and unauthorized caller share one anti-enumeration outcome. history_depth is the closed range 0..256 with default 0 and MUST NOT be silently capped; after_resolution_event_ref stops the disclosed segment exclusively at a known ancestor in this account's lineage and requires history_depth >= 1. A truncated segment sets history_complete=false and returns next_audit_cursor; omitted history is unknown, never absent.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. account_id is server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone.v1(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.

Authenticated client dispatch of private invite evidence through the inviter Station. invite_event_id must resolve to an Event already accepted by this service and authored by the current session actor. The service reads its own stored canonical Event bytes; local delivery reuses the peer receive policy path and remote delivery builds the peer request from those bytes.

Transaction-bound monotonic erasure of the exact old secret_storage series reserved by a SecurityRotationTransaction. Partial outcomes persist per series/object; exact retry never resurrects or rewrites an erased item. A complete outcome carries the sole canonical erase confirmation.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over. While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.
Issue a durable current-device-only challenge with lifetime at most 300 seconds. Recovery unlock reuses its recovery session challenge.
Same still-authorized holder exact replay returns the durable unlock outcome without charging the one-use challenge again.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the same empty success response, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Session-authenticated entry to the canonical KeyPackage claim carrier. The participant supplies the same closed device|agent requester_authorization and stable service_binding with source/destination service DIDs used by peer claim; deployment trust domains are absent from participant-authored bytes and are bound only by the Station's verified resolution plus outer RFC 9421 headers. The local Station verifies the current durable requester authorization and exact current joined-member ActorId routing projection; local source=destination uses the same destination-authority CAS, while remote targets are durably relayed without rewriting the participant-signed body. Uncertain outcomes are queried by the original claim_request_id and request digest before any exact resend.

Authenticated cross-account device directory and published prekey-bundle read. Selectors are bounded at 1..16 accounts and 32 devices each with a 64 KiB canonical request; an over-limit request fails whole. Disclosure requires a current authorization relationship - a Realm the requester still joins, or a current Contact/call/session context, where the Contact case never requires a shared Realm. Targets hosted by another Station are resolved through ak.peer.keys.read.lookup.v1 and verified locally before the row is returned; the client never contacts a foreign Station and its session credential is never forwarded. failures[].reason_code is the closed pair device_result_unavailable and device_directory_unavailable, and an unavailable fetch is never rendered as an empty device set.

Own-Station verified route and signing keys for the media service anchored by one joined Realm current accepted realm_media_service typed current result. Membership visibility and the anchored typed current result are evaluated under one confirmed basis with exactly one head per Realm; the caller supplies no service id, DID, base URL or candidate origin. The result resolves service identity, purpose and route only: it releases no media key, no backend token and no plaintext-visibility authorization, and expires_at bounds route and key reuse to at most 300 seconds. Invisible Realm or absent anchor returns not_found; unresolved accepted state returns temporarily_unavailable. Request and complete response canonical JSON are each bounded to 64 KiB.

Prepare one complete unsigned ak.message.create from a closed intent, after client encryption where required. Exact canonical request replay; expires at client created_at plus 300 seconds. No sequence reservation and no submit ticket.

durable_effect.rationale: Only a bounded expiring preparation cache; no accepted Event, sequence, membership or projection mutation.

operations.notes: Carries one caller-signed moderation report Event. The current governance Station revalidates the authenticated reporter, target visibility, effective scope and current authorization, then commits the exact Event on that scope's authority stream. The Event contains only its closed producer, scope, payload and signature fields.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Accepts exactly one caller-signed ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private Event. The Event payload is the complete ak.schema.read_cursor.v1 cursor; envelope.actor_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated holder, payload.device_id MUST equal the authenticated session device, and envelope.realm_id MUST equal payload.realm_id. The service validates and forwards the exact Event bytes and MUST NOT rebuild the payload or co-sign. The cursor object carries neither an id nor an updated_at — a cursor is never updated in place, its identity is the (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope) tuple and there is no read_cursor typed ID kind — so the update time of an advance is the Event envelope created_at, and the read_marker_outcome updated_at is that derived envelope time of the winning advance. Sibling devices observe the winner as the ak.read_cursor.update device message whose content is ak.schema.read_cursor_update.v1. Multi-device convergence is causal-first per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position that causally dominates the other wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only to causally concurrent positions, and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Prepares one join, knock or invite acceptance against the Realm's current governance Station. The Station is discovered from the current authority bundle, not from the inviter or genesis Station. Preparation freezes the exact request and current policy revision; final admission is an authority commit and performs no actor-checkpoint, RealmCommit-basis or authority-commit calculation.

Own-Station validated progress of one join application authored by this account before membership exists. account_id MUST equal the complete account of the authenticated session and its Station MUST be the service handling the request. origin_state reports this Station's own durable forwarding fact and is never Realm acceptance; realm_state appears only after a bounded candidate answered, and accepted_commit_id appears only when this Station has itself verified and accepted the covering RealmCommit. The outcome carries no Ack, authority set, authority signature or RealmCommit bytes: after committed the account is a member and continues through the ordinary member federation and sync surfaces. Unknown Event, another account's application and a non-matching session share one non-enumerating not_found.

Own-Station validated pre-join Realm preview. account_id MUST equal the complete account of the authenticated session and its Station MUST be the service handling the request. The invite target is resolved only against inviter_account_id.station_id, taking the equivalent local path when that Station is this service; every other target is resolved through the Directory discovery input surface and independently validated before it becomes a result. The client never calls the source, never selects a forwarding candidate and never goes back to a truth source: join_candidates, source_refs, stale and divergent are omitted. request_digest binds the exact chosen target, and source names where the disclosure came from. An unreachable source is a retryable upstream failure and MUST NOT be replaced by another service identity or another Realm member Station.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organization_ids hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hint_ids are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.

Registered repair-material read for one Relation primary conflict domain. The Station returns the frozen baseline (complete member_count plus the chained members_digest) and exactly one 256-member page of the canonically ordered candidate list; a page never takes effect alone, and the client walks every page in ascending page_index over the prev_page_digest chain before signing an ak.relation.resolve against that members_digest. The ordinary 16-head diagnostic bound governs only the optional diagnostic field and MUST NOT truncate, reorder or refuse this material: a group that already failed with relation_conflict_fanout_exceeded is exactly the group that needs it. The caller must be authorized to read every candidate in the group; a partially visible group returns relation_conflict_group_not_visible rather than a shortened list, and retained-but-unreadable material returns relation_conflict_material_unavailable instead of a truncated page. A chain break, gap, reorder or mid-read group change returns relation_conflict_material_page_gap and the read restarts at page_index=0.

Continues only the canonical next transaction step. Recovery's terminal step carries the replacement-device-signed recovery receipt; the current governance Station atomically validates both prepared producer Events, issues their PCR-stream RealmCommit, advances device generation, activates the device and consumes the session. The client never supplies or signs the RealmCommit.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the prepared plan, accepted step prefix and optional terminal result; callers derive the next action from kind plus prefix length. It MUST NOT synthesize progress from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.
Transient encrypted Signal rail. It creates no durable Event or RealmCommit, does not advance any authority stream, and grants no delivery or authorization proof.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.

Own Station validates 1..64 exact account-device/Agent current or historical selectors. Current keys serve this validation invocation only. Historical receiver is this authenticated recipient Station and the Event must be locally accepted and readable; Device and Agent history independently resolve the original producer key from portable immutable authorization evidence and apply known closure decisions. Request <=64 KiB; each result <=16 KiB; complete response <=1 MiB. Exactly one resolved/unavailable result per selector; no portable closure, caller-selected receiver, or current-directory substitution for history.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Purpose-scoped acceptance attestation the authenticated inviter obtains from its own Station for one exact ak.invite.third_party it authored (third-party-invites.md section 7.4). The Station evaluates its current accepted basis, confirms the caller authored the invite, that the invite typed current result is pending, and that verification_id matches the typed current result and the current allowlist, then signs an attestation binding station_id, verification_id, audience, realm_id, invite_id, inviter_account_id, provisioning_id, the exact public material, invite_expires_at, invite_state, accepted_commit_id, observed_at and its own expires_at. The caller supplies no governance material and receives no governance closure, RealmCommit ancestry or membership listing; the attestation authorizes nothing except activation of the named provisioning record. Not visible, not authored by the caller and not pending all return the uniform section 6 not_found; a basis the Station cannot currently confirm returns revision_unavailable.

success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Ordinary authoring and object changes follow registered data execution with verified cached authority. Risk tier does not impose RealmCommit age, online origin or periodic freshness on ordinary publication.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Registered high-risk approvals and explicit validity constraints are enforced. Security writes revalidate exact authority and preconditions in the unique confirmation sequence; risk labels do not override execution classification.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root typed current result may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

actions.notes: Authorizes a service-actor signed bridge error Event only for the exact active Applet installation, registration epoch and granted scope. The Event still carries applet_id and a real authorization_ref; service signature is provenance, not authority.

Authorizes only actor_role=ghost ak.applet.managed_actor.provision inside the closed four-Event Ghost unit: provision, applet_managed_control PCR genesis, accountability grant and profile create. The conditional Event admission and operation validator require the exact active registration/grant/scope and atomic set.

Reducer-materialized record of a Realm-link inheritance derivation (zh/models/realm-links.md section 6). No principal authors it and no principal can be granted it, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.

Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.member_id == envelope.actor_id using the complete ActorId and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.member_id != envelope.actor_id using the complete ActorId.

Authorizes only the transaction-bound old-series targets in a fixed SecurityRotationTransaction plan after both replacement active-series pointers are accepted. It never authorizes deleting an active or unplanned backup series.
Direct Conversation participant self-leave only. It never authorizes leave/ban/remove of the other participant or any join transition.

Accepted-at compensation for a self-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard leave transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it cannot be transferred or used as ordinary membership authority.

Accepted-at compensation for a delegated/admin-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard remove transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it grants no Realm admin capability.

Direct Conversation exact-pair self-rejoin only. It never authorizes a first join, a third participant, or a join authored on behalf of the other participant, and it never authorizes any grant, policy, admin, Strand or binding change.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects realm_alias). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3.

Terminal Realm lifecycle. Authored only by the current controller of the Realm authority-root typed current result with an independent destructive confirmation; it MUST NOT be granted to anyone, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Held either by the current controller of the realm_authority_root typed current result (root authority, not a grant) or by an ordinary revocable co-owner grant. Both derived sets are rule-generated; hand edits are rejected by tools/artifact_pipeline.py check.

Rotates the controller binding of the Realm authority-root typed current result. Authored only by the current controller with successor acceptance; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.
Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.

Adjudicating a whole Relation conflict domain decides one outcome for every candidate in the group, including candidates the actor did not author, so it is registered separately from the per-Relation write actions. The reducer MUST verify the grant covers every candidate and scope in the covered group; ak.relation.update or ak.relation.tombstone on one member never substitutes.
Holder-private consent is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm; it is never grantable to a Realm co-owner or another principal.
Holder-private consent revocation is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm and must remove caller-observed dots; it is never grantable.

Advances the Realm authority-root delegation generation, which invalidates every grant descending from a realm_root ref of the previous generation. Authored only by the current controller against the frozen pre-state digest; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set. profiles/conformance-profiles.json lists it in the root-owner mask's allowed_root_control_actions alongside ak.realm.owner.transfer.

registry_rules: A calendar schedule MUST carry a signed tzdb_version naming one release row below. Receivers resolve timezone and every derived instant with that release, never with their locally installed release.

Release rows are append-only and each row is frozen once published, including its own required_normalizations table, because historical schedules signed that row. Withdrawing a release is expressed by setting status=inactive, never by deleting or rewriting the row.

required_normalizations is per release, not global. A later IANA release that changes a Link target expresses that by carrying a different mapping in its own row; the earlier row keeps the mapping that was in force when those schedules were signed. A global table could not represent both at once and would silently break the append-only promise.

Determinism comes from the release tag: IANA tzdata release tags are immutable once published. This registry deliberately does not mirror the full Zone/Link table and does not pin a distribution digest, because a hand-copied mirror would drift from IANA and become a second truth source, and this repository cannot verify third-party distribution bytes. Deployments that additionally need supply-chain pinning verify the distribution in their own build; that pinning is out of scope for v1 interop.

Canonicalization is defined by the Link declarations of the pinned IANA release as published by IANA, in particular its backward and etcetera files: the canonical Zone is the Link target. It is NOT defined by whatever a given platform time zone library happens to expose, since distributions may build the same release with different link handling.

Producers MUST rewrite timezone to the canonical Zone before signing. Receivers MUST NOT re-canonicalize a signed value: an alias that reaches the wire is a producer defect and MUST be rejected, not repaired. The RSVP occurrence key reuses the exact signed timezone value.

Each row required_normalizations is the conformance-required subset that vectors pin for that release. It is not the full alias set; an input outside the table is still canonicalized by that release Link declarations.

Updating a schedule tzdb_version MAY change derived instants but MUST NOT change the signed timezone value or any local occurrence key. When any occurrence instant or end changes, the significant-change table requires RSVP needs_reconfirmation plus a schedule notification.

A service that cannot execute a schedule tzdb_version MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or unsupported_feature, or mark instant projection unresolved. Falling back to a nearby or newer release is forbidden. Services declare their executable set in ServiceDescribe.calendar_tzdb_versions.

releases.notes: v1 conformance baseline release. Frozen: this row required_normalizations is the mapping schedules pinned to 2025a were signed against.
Appended release; schedules pinned to it expand with its rules only. Its required_normalizations is identical to 2025a because no listed Link target changed between the two releases.

Every W3C DID Document member normatively consumed by Arkret MUST appear in known_members and MUST survive projection into normalized_document_schema_ref

Resolve the exact accepted-at historical DID Document version and read normalized metadata.primary_handle for deterministic primary-handle selection.

registry_rules: Only an active adapter row can validate a did or project it to did_core_id. DID syntax alone never admits a method.
project is a method-defined semantic transform over a canonical bare did, not generic string concatenation or prefix removal. Receivers compare the complete projected did_core_id byte-for-byte.

Every adapter validates method-native control, deactivation, currentness and history evidence according to its trust profile before returning a verified projection. Unknown methods and unknown adapter versions fail closed.

A new did is an update of an existing principal or service only when the same active adapter projects it to the identical did_core_id. A method or core change creates a new identity and cannot inherit authorization through a continuity assertion.
DID URLs are constructed and compared from the verified did under the adapter's DID URL rules. A did_core_id is never used as a DID URL base.

No adapter exposes expand or core_to_did. Even when a method-specific suffix appears reversible, an isolated did_core_id cannot create resolution authority; the required did or did_url arrives through did-evidence-boundary-registry.json.

A did is a canonical bare DID and therefore contains no path, query or fragment. Each active adapter deterministically emits method_history_head, version_id and service_resolution_event_ref according to its registered rules, including synthetic values for methods without native history.

For a generic Event proof, the verifier extracts the canonical bare did base from proof.verification_method, validates the active adapter and key at the cited accepted-at method history, projects that did, and compares the resulting did_core_id to executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery are the only registered special admissions and never convert current DID control into generic human PCR authority.

A principal resolution update is admitted only in its derived identity-control Realm and only when one exact expected_revision precondition guards ak:result:identity_resolution:null. The guarded whole resolution_projection MUST equal the accepted current typed current result; predecessor event/history coordinates come only from that signed precondition, never from payload mirrors.

Exactly one active adapter, did:webvh:1.0, carries human_principal_anchor=true and declares registration_anchor_kind=webvh_registration; that value is the sole discriminator of the closed principal-registration-anchor contract. A human principal is registered, given PCR genesis and later replayed from a portable account_device_control root only through that branch. Every other method, including did:key and did:web, carries human_principal_anchor=false and MUST fail closed with unsupported_did_method at schema and role admission, before any method parser, history replay or registry write. Adding another human anchor requires a newly registered portable publication-proof or independent-witness trust model with its own threat model and conformance vectors; it MUST NOT enter through a test fixture, an optional sidecar member or a locally widened allowlist.

payload.next is a method-valid successor of precondition.value.method_history_head

project(resolution_projection.did) == principal_id
method_history_evidence boundary and currentness validate under the adapter selected by resolution_projection.did
principal_genesis_event.kind == ak.realm.create and principal_genesis_event is resolution head 0
principal_genesis_event.actor_id == principal_id
principal_genesis_event.payload.object.purpose is principal_control, agent_control or applet_managed_control

if current_resolution_event is principal_genesis_event then predecessor_resolution_events is empty; otherwise predecessor_resolution_events[0] is the current Event's guarded immediate predecessor when history_depth is nonzero

the supplied resolution events form a contiguous immediate-predecessor segment backward from current_resolution_event under the exact guarded whole-typed current result values; the segment never exceeds request history_depth items and never skips an intermediate Event

history_complete is true exactly when the segment terminates at principal_genesis_event or at the exclusive request after_resolution_event_ref ancestor; otherwise history_complete is false, next_audit_cursor equals value.resolution_event_ref in the exact expected_revision precondition of the oldest supplied Event (its guarded immediate predecessor), and omitted history is never treated as absent
accepted_commit.realm_id == principal_control_realm_id and accepted_commit recursively covers both principal_genesis_event.event_digest and current_resolution_event.event_digest
the registered resolution reducer applied to current_resolution_event yields the response's current resolution projection and project(did) == principal_id
method_history_evidence boundary and currentness validate under the adapter selected by that current resolution projection's did

portable.relocation_rule: A successor whose canonical host-and-path differs from the accepted predecessor is valid only when the predecessor's effective portable value is true and every method-native successor check succeeds. Missing or false rejects relocation; setting portable=true only in the relocating successor cannot authorize that same relocation.

watchers.rule: The adapter validates and retains watchers as method-native canonical data, but v1 never uses it for authorization, admission, controller selection, witness quorum, freshness, routing or policy. Unknown shape still fails under the method parser; presence, absence or contents cannot grant authority.

entries.description: Mandatory Arkret v1 core HTTPS JSON/NDJSON binding.
Optional HTTPS tus companion binding; operation coverage comes only from advertised operation bundles.
Optional authenticated multiplexed WebSocket binding; operation coverage comes only from advertised operation bundles.

feature_registry.description: Canonical exact feature identities advertised only through ServiceDescribe.supported_features.
registry_rules: Every standard feature id is registered here and ends in .v1; unregistered ak.feature.* values are invalid.
supported_features is the only public runtime feature claim set. Registry status describes lifecycle and never creates a second advertised set.
A feature cannot make an operation available; every required operation pair must already be present in the union of advertised operation bundles.
A feature cannot widen a selected operation schema. Contract-shape changes require a distinct versioned operation identity.

semantic_guarantees: Agent runtime approval transitions emit the normative user-visible notification surface.
Detached JWS inputs and verification results follow the canonical Arkret detached-signature transcript.
Identity resolution verifies and serves the native did:webvh log contract.
Invite addressing accepts only the registered introduction kinds and advertised maximum-behavior policy.
Message bodies accept the versioned Content Block structural contract.

Last-resort KeyPackages follow the replay, consumption, and rotation rules of the normative MLS contract. Expiry bounds new distribution eligibility only; captured Welcome confidentiality is not restored by expiry or rotation, and future epoch recovery depends on effective secret updates and the MLS threat conditions.
The deployment can emit the normative notification projection without implying push transport support.

current_result_registry.description: Closed typed current-result families derived from authority-committed Events. Selectors are domain types, never alternate typed current result IDs.
